section_heading: SECTION 6 DRYDOCKS, FLOATING DOCKS, SYNCROLIFTS AND SLIPWAYS
plain_summary: This page introduces Section 6, which covers drydocks, floating docks, syncrolifts, and slipways. It defines 'Ordinary working hours' for the Ports of Cape Town, East London, and Durban, and outlines conditions for 'Week-ends and Public Holidays' work. Crucially, it details how the 'Tonnage of vessels for tariff purposes' is calculated, including a conversion factor and an alternative method if a tonnage certificate is unavailable. Finally, it lists the booking fees (deposits) required for drydocks and syncrolifts at the Ports of Cape Town and East London.

formulas.formula_as_written: The gross tonnage of a vessel in cubic metres (conversion factor 2,83) of a vessel as per the tonnage certificate issued in terms of the Tonnage Convention 1969, Plus The tonnage is mass, of all cargo on board. Where the vessel's tonnage certificate is not available the highest tonnage as reflected in Lloyds Register of Shipping converted (x2,83) to cubic metres is accepted.
formulas.what_it_calculates: Tonnage of vessels for tariff purposes
parameters_used: mass of all cargo on board
formulas.rounding_or_conditions: Conversion factor 2,83. If tonnage certificate is not available, use highest tonnage from Lloyds Register of Shipping converted (x2,83) to cubic metres.

ambiguities_or_risks: The definition of 'Ordinary working hours' for Ports of Cape Town and East London as 'According to the custom of the facility' is vague and requires external knowledge.

The calculation for 'Tonnage of vessels for tariff purposes' states 'Plus The tonnage is mass, of all cargo on board.' which implies addition to the gross tonnage, but the exact method of combining these two components (GT in cubic metres and cargo mass) could be interpreted differently without further clarification on units or conversion.
